title: Chitosan supplementation enhances antimicrobial proteins in the mouse small intestine
content:
Abstract

Background

Chitosan is a partially deacetylated derivative of chitin with distinct physicochemical properties, but its effects on intestinal epithelial defense remain unclear. This study investigated whether dietary chitosan and chitin regulate antimicrobial protein expression in the mouse small intestine and examined the underlying mechanisms. Female C57BL/6J mice were fed control, chitin-supplemented, or chitosan-supplemented diets.

Results

Chitosan, but not chitin, markedly altered jejunal gene expression and increased the mRNA and protein expression of resistin-like molecule β (RELMβ) and small proline-rich protein 2A (SPRR2A). Chitosan supplementation also increased Il13, Tslp, and Mcpt1 expression and enhanced signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6) phosphorylation, indicating activation of type 2 immune responses. In tuft cell-deficient Pou2f3-knockout mice, chitosan failed to increase RELMβ and SPRR2A protein levels, STAT6 phosphorylation, or the expression of Il13, Tslp, and Mcpt1.

Conclusion

These findings indicate that dietary chitosan enhances intestinal antimicrobial protein expression through a tuft cell-dependent type 2 immune response and STAT6 signaling. Chitosan may therefore represent a dietary factor that modulates intestinal epithelial defense. © 2026 The Author(s).
